Deloitte (2022). A Roadmap for Decarbonising Australian Alumina Refining. Prepared for the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA), in collaboration with ARENA and in consultation with Alcoa, Rio Tinto and South32. November 2022. No DOI or report number printed (design file RITM1115764). Publisher/author is Deloitte, not ARENA; the id arena_2022_001 was replaced by deloitte_2022_001.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed page + 9). A qualitative sector roadmap: it has almost no unit costs. Loaded: Table 4.1 (TRL per technology, capex class: $$ up to ~$700M, $$$ above $700M for a greenfield facility, loaded as upper or lower bound), the pilot and demonstration cost estimates of Figure ii and Figure 7.1 (MVR 4 MW pilot $35M, 40 MW deployment $170M, electric calcination 0.2-2 t/h pilot $20M, 20-120 t/h demonstrations $50-250M, hydrogen full-scale calciner $50-250M excluding hydrogen), derived per-kW and per-t figures from the printed ratings, the Australian average emissions intensity 0.71 t CO2e/t, digestion steam conditions (175-230 degC at 600-800 kPa low-temperature; 325-400 degC at 5,000-10,000 kPa high-temperature), calcination energy 3 GJ/t, reduction potentials (MVR up to 70% of refinery emissions; MVR plus electric or hydrogen calcination up to 98%), CST steam and tower temperatures. In _other-values: 10.5 GJ/t average energy, energy shares, primary energy 9.8 vs 4.6 GJ/t, pilot funding, hydrogen price threshold. Not loaded: market, regulatory and ecosystem chapters, emissions trajectories, workshop findings. There is NO capex or opex per unit of capacity, no energy use or abatement cost per tonne for MVR, electric boilers, hydrogen or biomass options. Traps: (1) currency is printed only as "$" (AUD assumed) with no price year. (2) The Alcoa MVR case-study text prints a $35 million project; a hidden text layer of the same paragraph carries $28.2 million. (3) The Alcoa Wagerup and Pinjarra items are projects, not unit costs; MW basis of the MVR figures is not printed (electric input assumed). (4) 98% reduction applies to low-temperature refineries only. (5) Energy intensities 10.5 GJ/t (Australian average, all energy) and 9.8 GJ/t (primary energy in the future-state comparison) are different bases.
